Don Brown retained his title, as was generally expected, but Bill Treacher (2nd), Len Fletcher (3rd) and Harry Churcher (4th) all finished inside 14 mins. 26 secs.

Tommy Green, young as ever, and Len Fletcher, who we were all glad to see on the road once again, and Bill Treacher, completed our team. Our score was the very low one of 19 points; and second came Surrey Walking Club, with 73 points.

Bill Treacher took the special prize for the first man to finish, not gaining any other award, from the club with the largest number of starters, and our "B" team took the third team handicap prizes and consisted of A.
W.C.) and Bill Treacher, our Track vice-captain. Bill was content to remain in second place, preferring caution and second placing, than to risk disqualification and loss of points.
Boddington, just holding off Harry Churcher and Bill Treacher, for third position.
The 2 Miles Walk saw Bill Treacher and Harry Churcher having a battle royal throughout and it was only down the straight that the former just forged to the front, and so won a very fine race.

When these men are joined by others, such as Don Brown, Fred Bentley, Bill Treacher, Len Storey, Jack Rutland, Reg. Elson, Eddie Heather and others, we may be sure our "Junior and "Senior" teams will command respect.
Len Coleman and Bill Treacher were battling for third place until Treacher was disqualified at 1½ miles. Harry was a little too fast for Joe, and won in 14 min. 36 sec.

Charlie Churcher, after having steadily worked his way into a useful position, suffered disqualification. Alan Bridger and Bill Treacher also shared a similar fate. This reduced our "A" team to four (seven only starting).
